prompt.context: Your client is a Major Magazine Publisher. Currently, they own a Women's magazine (similar to Cosmopolitan) and a Personal Finance magazine (similar to Fortune). They are considering launching a new magazine about Fine Living, targeted to Wealthy Males (similar to GQ).
prompt.question: What is the market size, and should they launch the new Fine Living magazine?

clarifying_info.q: Is there a goal the company is trying to reach with the launch?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the company would like to hit $10M in annual revenue.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company have the resources to launch a new magazine?
Is the new magazine offered only in print, or online as well?
clarifying_info.a: It will be offered only in print.

clarifying_info.q: In what ways can the magazine be purchased?
clarifying_info.a: It is offered as a yearly subscription (12 issues per year) and can also be bought retail one issue at a time.

clarifying_info.q: What is the target geography for the magazine?
clarifying_info.a: It will be offered in the U.S. only.

clarifying_info.q: What are the costs of the magazine?
clarifying_info.a: Costs can be ignored in this analysis.

framework: Q1: Estimate market size in number of people (target segment)
Q2: Convert to market size in dollars using subscription and retail revenue assumptions
Q3: Assess whether the client should launch (profitability vs. goal, competition, market share, risks)

questions.prompt: Q1: What is the market size in people?
questions.guidance: Start with U.S. population, filter to males, apply age segmentation, then apply wealth percentages to each relevant age band. Age 0-20 is excluded as too young.

math.setup: 300M U.S. population → 50% male = 150M males. Split evenly into 4 age bands (0-20, 21-40, 41-60, 61-80) = 37.5M each. Exclude 0-20. Apply wealth % to remaining bands.

questions.prompt: Q2: What is the market size in dollars?
questions.guidance: Split total readers 50/50 between subscription and retail. Calculate annual revenue for each channel using different price-per-issue and issue frequency assumptions.

math.setup: 9.4M total readers split 50/50: 4.7M subscribers, 4.7M retail customers. Subscription: 12 issues/year at $3/issue. Retail: 4 issues/year at $5/issue.

questions.prompt: Q3: Should the client launch the new magazine?
questions.guidance: Use the market size figure to estimate client revenue based on capturable market share, then compare to the $10M revenue goal. Factor in competition and market growth.

math.setup: Survey data shows client can capture 5% of the $263.2M market. Market is not growing. Competition: GQ holds 60%, other/fragmented 40%.
math.answer: $13.16M projected annual revenue, exceeding the $10M goal

recommendation: The client should move forward with the launch of the new Fine Living magazine. Expected revenue of ~$13.6M per year exceeds the stated goal of $10M per year.
risks: Costs need to remain below $3.6M (the buffer above the $10M goal). Costs may include fixed costs for manufacturing, R&D for new topic/content, etc.
Cannibalization risk: the Fine Living/Wealthy Male audience may overlap with the existing Personal Finance magazine audience, potentially cannibalizing existing revenues.
Market is not growing, so share gains must come from competitors.
next_steps: Conduct detailed cost analysis to confirm costs stay under $3.6M.
Analyze content overlap with the Personal Finance magazine to quantify cannibalization risk.
Identify cost synergies across the portfolio (manufacturing, marketing, distribution) that the addition of a third magazine may unlock.
